items.title: Smooth fibre bundles and local trivializations
Smooth vector bundles, rank, fibres, and trivial bundles
A vector bundle projection is a surjective submersion
items.strategy: In a local trivialization the bundle projection becomes the product projection U x R^r -> U. The differential of that projection is the coordinate projection, so the submersion claim is local and transports back through the trivialization.

items.title: Vector bundle charts and transition functions
Vector bundle transition functions satisfy the cocycle identities
Construction of a vector bundle from a smooth cocycle
items.strategy: Start from the countable disjoint union of the local trivial pieces, impose the cocycle relation, and then verify directly that the quotient charts are bijective with smooth overlaps. The proof keeps Hausdorffness and second countability explicit instead of treating the quotient as automatically manifold-shaped.

items.title: Isomorphic cocycles define isomorphic vector bundles
items.strategy: A gauge family h_alpha acts fibrewise on each local trivial piece. The cocycle conjugacy relation is exactly what makes those local maps descend to a well-defined global bundle isomorphism on the quotient.

items.title: Restrictions of vector bundles
The zero section is a smooth embedding
items.strategy: In each vector bundle chart the zero section is the coordinate inclusion p |-> (p,0). Local triviality therefore reduces smoothness and the embedding condition to the standard slice embedding in a product chart.

items.title: The total space of a rank-r bundle has dimension dim M + r
Smooth sections, local sections, and support
Local and global frames of a vector bundle
Local frames and local trivializations are equivalent data
items.strategy: Given a local frame, use unique coordinates in each fibre to build the trivialization map to R^r; given a trivialization, pull back the standard basis vectors to get a local frame. The change-of-basis matrix on overlaps is the same matrix that appears in the bundle transition law.

items.title: A vector bundle is trivial if and only if it has a global frame
Smoothness of a section is equivalent to smooth local components
items.strategy: Write a section in a local frame as a coordinate tuple of scalar functions. Because the trivialization and its inverse are smooth, section smoothness is exactly smoothness of those component functions.

items.title: Smooth sections form a module over smooth functions
Every vector in a fibre extends to a compactly supported smooth section
items.strategy: Choose a local frame around the base point, prescribe constant local coordinates realizing the chosen fibre vector, and then multiply by a bump function supported inside the trivializing neighborhood.

items.title: Locally finite linear combinations of sections are smooth
items.strategy: In a local frame, the linear combination reduces to a locally finite sum of smooth scalar component functions. Smoothness is then the previously proved locally finite smooth-sum statement, checked coordinatewise.

items.title: Vector bundle maps over a smooth base map
Smoothness of a bundle map is equivalent to smooth local matrices
items.strategy: Choose local frames on source and target, express the fibrewise linear map by a matrix of scalar coefficient functions, and compare the bundle map with the induced matrix-valued coordinate representative in the trivializations.

items.title: A fibrewise bijective smooth bundle map over a diffeomorphism is a bundle isomorphism
items.strategy: In local trivializations the map has the form (p,v) |-> (f(p),A(p)v) with A(p) invertible on every fibre. The inverse is therefore (q,w) |-> (f^-1(q),A(f^-1(q))^-1 w), and smoothness comes from smooth inversion on the general linear locus together with the smooth base inverse.

items.title: Vector subbundles
Constant-rank kernels and images of bundle maps over one base are subbundles
items.strategy: Fix a local matrix representative with one nonzero rank minor constant on a neighborhood, solve for the dependent coordinates, and use those coordinates to build smooth local frames for the kernel and image. The image statement is kept over a common base, and the later pullback reformulation handles the general map-over-f case.

items.title: Pullback vector bundles as fibre products
The pullback fibre product is a smooth vector bundle
items.strategy: Restrict each bundle trivialization over U to the fibre product over f^-1(U), which gives a direct identification with f^-1(U) x R^r. The resulting overlap maps are exactly the pulled-back transition matrices g_ba o f, so the atlas and its independence are explicit.

items.title: Pullback is functorial up to canonical bundle isomorphism
items.strategy: The identity and composite pullbacks are matched by the obvious fibrewise maps on pairs, and the equalities needed for well-definedness are the defining fibre-product equations. Smoothness is checked in the pulled-back trivializations from the previous theorem.

items.title: Whitney sums of vector bundles
Whitney sums are smooth vector bundles
items.strategy: On a common trivializing neighborhood, identify E and F with U x R^r and U x R^s, and then identify their fibrewise direct sum with U x (R^r oplus R^s). The transition law is block diagonal, so the bundle atlas is immediate once the local model is written honestly.

items.title: Dual and Hom vector bundles
Dual and Hom transition functions define smooth bundles
items.strategy: Dual bundle transitions are the inverse transpose of the original transition matrices, while Hom transitions are A |-> h A g^-1. Those operations are algebraic in the matrix entries on the general linear locus, so the bundle structures follow from the original smooth transition data.

items.title: Sections of Hom are the same as smooth fibrewise linear maps
items.strategy: A section of Hom(E,F) is a smoothly varying choice of a linear map on each fibre, and in a pair of local frames its coordinates are exactly the matrix entries of the corresponding bundle map. The correspondence is therefore obtained by reading the same local matrix in two languages.

items.title: Bundle maps over f are sections of the pulled-back Hom bundle
items.strategy: A bundle map E -> F over f picks, for each p in M, a linear map E_p -> F_f(p), which is exactly an element of Hom(E_p,(f^*F)_p). Passing to local trivializations shows that smoothness of the bundle map matches smoothness of the resulting section.

items.title: Quotient vector bundles by a subbundle
A vector bundle quotient by a subbundle is a smooth vector bundle
items.strategy: Choose adapted local frames in which the first k frame vectors span the subbundle. Quotient coordinates are then read off from the remaining frame vectors, and the proof checks that changing adapted frames induces the same quotient smooth structure.

items.title: The canonical map to a quotient bundle is a smooth bundle map
Smooth bundle metrics
Every smooth vector bundle admits a smooth bundle metric
items.strategy: Choose local frames, pull back the Euclidean inner product on each trivial patch, and average those local metrics with a subordinate smooth partition of unity. The convex combination is fibrewise positive definite because the weights are nonnegative and sum to one.

items.title: Orthogonal complements of subbundles are smooth subbundles
items.strategy: In a local frame extending a frame of the subbundle, apply smooth Gram-Schmidt to obtain a local orthonormal frame adapted to the metric. The orthogonal complement is then spanned by the remaining frame vectors, which proves both smoothness and constant rank.

items.title: Every vector subbundle has a smooth complement
Every short exact sequence of smooth vector bundles splits
items.strategy: Identify the image of the monomorphism with a smooth subbundle of the middle bundle, choose a smooth complement, and then use the quotient map to identify that complement with the target bundle. The argument yields existence of a splitting and avoids any claim of canonicity.

items.title: Normal and conormal bundles of an embedded submanifold
Normal and conormal bundles are smooth vector bundles
items.strategy: In slice coordinates the tangent bundle along the submanifold splits into tangent and normal coordinate directions, so the tangent restriction contains a visible smooth subbundle and the quotient is locally trivial. The same coordinates show that the annihilator of the tangent directions is a smooth conormal subbundle of the restricted cotangent bundle.

items.title: An ambient Riemannian metric identifies the normal quotient with the orthogonal normal bundle
items.strategy: Use the metric to split TM|_S as TS oplus TS^⊥ and then restrict the canonical quotient map to the orthogonal complement. Fibrewise this is the standard quotient-by-a-complement isomorphism, and smoothness follows from the smooth complement bundle just constructed.

items.title: Assuming countable choice, every smooth manifold admits a Riemannian metric
A vector bundle section with surjective vertical differential at every zero has a submanifold zero set
items.strategy: Choose a local frame near a zero so the section becomes a smooth map to R^r. At a zero the extra derivative term from a frame change vanishes, so surjectivity of the vertical differential is trivialization-independent; the zero set is then a regular level set of the local component map.

items.title: Every vector bundle is globally trivial
items.strategy: The Mobius line bundle has local trivializations but no global nonvanishing frame, so the global triviality claim fails even in rank one over the circle.

items.title: A continuous fibrewise linear map over a smooth base map is automatically smooth
items.strategy: On a trivial line bundle, multiplication by a continuous but nonsmooth scalar function is fibrewise linear and continuous, but its local matrix coefficient is not smooth, so the bundle map is not smooth.

items.title: The fibrewise quotient of a vector bundle by arbitrary varying subspaces is a vector bundle
items.strategy: Without constant rank and smooth local frames, the quotient fibres can jump dimension and no smooth local trivialization survives. The constant-rank subbundle hypothesis in the quotient theorem is therefore essential.

items.title: A short exact sequence of vector bundles has a canonical splitting
items.strategy: A bundle metric yields a complement and hence a splitting, but the construction depends on that auxiliary choice. The splitting corollary proves existence only, not naturality.

items.title: The orthogonal normal bundle of a submanifold is defined without a metric
items.strategy: Only the quotient normal bundle and the conormal annihilator are intrinsic at this stage. The orthogonal complement depends on a chosen ambient metric, as the metric-identification proposition makes explicit.

items.title: The pullback bundle is the set-theoretic inverse image of the total space
items.strategy: The pullback retains both the new base point and the old fibre element, so it is a fibre product, not an inverse-image subset of the original total space.

title: Smooth Vector Bundles and Sections — Examples

items.title: The trivial line bundle and its sections as functions
items.strategy: A section of M x R over M is exactly a smooth function M -> R, because the bundle condition forces the first component to be the identity and the second component is arbitrary smooth scalar data.

items.title: The Mobius line bundle from a transition function
items.strategy: Cover S^1 by two arcs, glue trivial line bundles with transition function -1 on one overlap component and +1 on the other, and invoke the cocycle construction. The resulting line bundle is locally trivial but not globally framed.

items.title: The tautological line bundle over real projective space
items.strategy: On the standard affine patches of real projective space, use the distinguished nonzero coordinate to choose a local generator of the line represented by [x]. The overlap quotients give the transition functions and exhibit the bundle explicitly.

items.title: Assuming countable choice, the tangent and cotangent bundles are smooth vector bundles
The normal bundle of the sphere in Euclidean space is trivial
items.strategy: The outward radial unit field gives a nowhere-zero normal vector at every point of the sphere. It therefore supplies a global frame of the normal line bundle and proves triviality.

items.title: The tangent bundle of the circle is trivial
items.strategy: Use the unit tangent field obtained by rotating each point of S^1 by ninety degrees. This global nowhere-zero section is a global frame of the rank-one tangent bundle.

items.title: The hairy-ball theorem for even-dimensional spheres
Pullback of the tautological line bundle along the antipodal cover
items.strategy: Pull the tautological line bundle on RP^n back along the quotient map S^n -> RP^n and write the pullback points as pairs (x,(x,t x)). The scalar t gives an explicit nowhere-zero section, so the pulled-back line bundle is trivial.

items.title: The graph of a bundle map as a subbundle of a Whitney sum
items.strategy: For a bundle map Phi:E->F over the identity, its graph in E oplus F is locally the graph of a smooth matrix-valued map, hence is spanned by the frame vectors e_i oplus Phi(e_i). This gives a concrete smooth subbundle model for graphs.

items.title: A rank-jumping kernel is not a vector subbundle
items.strategy: Multiplication by x on the trivial line bundle over R has zero kernel away from 0 and one-dimensional kernel at 0. The fibre dimensions therefore jump, so the kernel cannot be a smooth vector subbundle.
